claims.text: Reiner–Woo–Yong, arXiv:0809.2981v2, state that the outside-box Schur classes form an ideal \(I_{r,n-r}\), induce \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\), and that \(\{s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\) is a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis. claims.text: For a bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), Bruhat comparison among \(r\)-Grassmannian permutations is partition inclusion; consequently \(J_v\) is generated as an ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2@L1354-L1375|claim=formal-document]

Theorem 5.4 is integral: for a type-\(A_{n-1}\) bigrassmannian with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), it gives two ideal-generating families in \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), where \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-2@L1380-L1401|claim=formal-document]

The source retains the project’s trajectory: minimality of both Theorem 5.4 families is explicitly conjectural, while the stronger assertion \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) is stated only as suspected. [source-2@L1495-L1502|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1517-L1552|claim=formal-document]

claims.text: The retrieved external-provider candidates contain no exact theorem text relevant to Grassmannian box quotients or integral Schur spans; the arXiv candidates identified concern path integrals or trajectory-data mining, not Schubert calculus. [arxiv:2112.15391v3; arxiv:2403.14151v2]

The supplied primary-source locator proves ideal generation by the containing-box Schur classes, but does not itself explicitly state the stronger equality \(J_v=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r}\mathbb Zs_\mu\). Establishing that equality still requires an integral multiplication-closure argument (for example via Littlewood–Richardson multiplication).
